note: Revised from the species-level description in Chhotani (1997), originally in English; the original treats the soldier and the worker, records the alate as unknown and does not describe the nymph. The soldier section gives the general measurements of the species, while the Other section records the measurements and condition of the lectotype, and literature citations, figure numbers and distribution records have been omitted.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule yellow to yellowish brown, darker anteriorly; antennae yellow; labrum yellowish brown; mandibles nearly black; remainder of the body yellow. Head sparsely setose, body more densely so. Total body length 4.0–6.0 mm. Head capsule elongate, subrectangular; sides nearly straight and parallel; in profile the posterior part nearly straight and the anterior part slightly inclined; width nearly half the length or slightly more; length to mandibular base 1.6–1.8 mm, maximum width 0.85–0.90 mm, width/length ratio 0.50–0.53. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 shortest. Postclypeus subcircular, distinctly delimited from the frons. Labrum broad, tongue-shaped, length 0.20–0.23 mm, width 0.23–0.25 mm; apex with a weak point, a pair of setae near the apex and several others on the body. Mandibles thick, short, stout, finely serrate; shorter than half the head length to the mandibular base; left mandible 0.75–0.78 mm long, ratio of left mandible length to head length 0.43–0.48. Postmentum rod-shaped; waist below the middle, about two-thirds of the maximum width; length 1.13–1.25 mm, maximum width 0.30–0.33 mm, waist width 0.18–0.20 mm. Pronotum saddle-shaped; anterior margin with a weak notch, posterior margin nearly straight; length 0.30–0.35 mm, width 0.53–0.60 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule, antennae and postclypeus pale yellow; remainder of the body still paler. Total body length 3.0 mm. Head capsule subquadrate, length to mandibular base 0.80 mm, width 0.85 mm. Antennae 13-segmented, segment 3 shortest. Postclypeus strongly convex, setose; posterior part projecting backwards, anterior part straight; length 0.23 mm, width 0.50 mm. Pronotum saddle-shaped, with no notch on either the anterior or the posterior margin; length 0.20 mm, width 0.40 mm. Measurements from a single worker preserved in alcohol (tube 17).

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The lectotype is the upper soldier on the pin, designated by Emerson in 1957; the remaining soldier and one worker are paralectotypes. Lectotype total body length 4.7 mm, head length to lateral base 1.80 mm, maximum head width 0.90 mm, head height 0.75 mm, left and right mandibles 0.78 and 0.75 mm long, postmentum length 1.25 mm, maximum width 0.33 mm, waist width 0.20 mm, pronotum length 0.35 mm, width 0.60 mm. The antennae of the lectotype are incomplete, with only 11 segments preserved; the fore legs are broken and the remaining legs are pressed beneath the venter.
